title: MetaPTP: An Adaptive Meta-optimized Model for Personalized Spatial Trajectory Prediction

problem.claim: Personalized spatial trajectory prediction must handle cold-start routes or users under sparse data conditions.

gap.claim: Existing meta-learning models use the same initialization for all tasks and therefore cannot fit users with varying travel preferences well.

contributions.claim: MetaPTP uses soft clustering to guide network initialization at finer granularity and transfer shared knowledge across users with similar travel preferences.
The model introduces a trajectory sampling method that constructs support sets using user preference and spatial trace similarities for task-related adaptation information.
A weight generator adaptively weights support-set trajectories according to user preferences and spatial distributions during fine-tuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on two real-world datasets.
The authors report that MetaPTP demonstrates superiority over comparison methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatial trajectory prediction supports a broad range of location-based applications.
Existing methods perform well on personal frequent routes when massive historical data is available.
Sparse data creates cold-start routes or users, while uniform meta-learning initialization fails to accommodate varying travel preferences.
MetaPTP combines preference-aware soft-clustered initialization, similarity-based support-set sampling, and adaptive trajectory weighting.
Experiments on two real-world datasets are reported to show model superiority.
